items.title: SkillOpt: Agent Skills as Trainable Parameters — Microsoft Research Achieves +23.5 Point Average Improvement Across 52 Evaluation Cells
items.title_zh: SkillOpt：将Agent技能参数化为可训练参数 — 微软研究院在52个评估单元中平均提升23.5分
items.summary: Microsoft Research proposes SkillOpt (Jun 30), treating agent skill files as trainable parameters outside a frozen model, with a full training loop: forward pass (batch execution), backward pass (trajectory reflection), bounded text edits, validation gating, rejected-edit feedback, and epoch-wise slow/meta updates. Evaluated across 6 benchmarks, 7 models (from GPT-5.5 to Qwen3.5-4B), and 3 execution modes (direct chat, Codex, Claude Code), SkillOpt was best or tied-for-best in all 52 evaluation cells. Average six-benchmark score rose from 58.8 to 82.3 (+23.5). Skills transfer across model scales and harnesses: a spreadsheet skill trained in Codex lifted Claude Code from 22.1 to 81.8. Only 1-4 accepted edits yield compact ~920-token skill files. Open-source at github.com/microsoft/SkillOpt.

items.title: Project Fetch Phase Two: Claude Opus 4.7 Operates Robodog Autonomously, 20x Faster Than Human Teams
items.title_zh: Project Fetch第二阶段：Claude Opus 4.7自主操控机器狗，比人类团队快20倍
items.summary: Anthropic revisited Project Fetch: Claude Opus 4.7 operated a robotic quadruped without human assistance and was ~20x faster than the fastest human team from Phase One on all completed tasks. The model was ~37x faster than the team without Claude. However, Claude still struggled with precise physical manipulation (beach ball retrieval). The trajectory mirrors coding agents: 'models helpful to humans → humans helpful to models → models do it themselves,' suggesting the early era of physical agentic AI.

items.title: Paving the Way for AI Agents in Biology: Deterministic Retrieval Layers Make Scientific Agents Reliable (VirBench + gget virus)
items.title_zh: 为生物学AI Agent铺路：确定性检索层让科学Agent可靠（VirBench基准 + gget virus工具）
items.summary: Anthropic studied how AI agents perform on viral sequence retrieval from NCBI Virus. Even frontier models (Claude, GPT-5.5, Biomni) achieved only 16-91% accuracy on VirBench due to brittle biological data infrastructure. Adding gget virus, a deterministic retrieval layer, raised accuracy to near 100% and eliminated run-to-run variability. Quantified real-world impact: inconsistent NCBI Virus retrievals shifted inferred Ebola outbreak TMRCA from 2014 to 1922. Preprint, benchmark, and tool are public.

items.title: Coding Agents in the Social Sciences: 1,260-Researcher Survey Finds 20% Adoption, Sharp Disparities
items.title_zh: 社会科学中的编程Agent：1260名研究者调查发现20%采用率，存在显著差异
items.summary: Anthropic surveyed 1,260 quantitative social scientists (Feb-Mar 2026). 81% have tried AI chatbots, but only 20% adopted coding agents (Claude Code 86% dominant). Adoption gap: economists 39% vs public health 6%; men 2x women; top-university researchers 40% more likely. Coding agent users post more working papers and grants but not yet more journal submissions. Most common uses: coding (97% of agent users), editing prose, methods advice.

items.title: Mapping AI-Enabled Cyber Threats: Google DeepMind's LLM ATT&CK Navigator for Agent Security
items.title_zh: AI赋能网络威胁图谱：Google DeepMind发布LLM ATT&CK Navigator用于Agent安全
items.summary: Google DeepMind announced the LLM ATT&CK Navigator, a framework for mapping and understanding AI-enabled cyber threats. The tool provides a structured way to assess how LLM agents could be exploited for offensive cyber operations and how to defend against them. Published alongside a policy analysis of a year's worth of AI cyber threat data.

items.title: Anthropic Economic Index: Cadences — Hourly Analysis of When People Use Claude, What They Produce, and AI's Impact on Work
items.title_zh: Anthropic经济指数：Cadences报告 — 按小时分析Claude使用模式与AI对工作的影响
items.summary: Anthropic's June 2026 Economic Index report samples hourly for the first time, analyzing when people use Claude, what they produce, and how they perceive AI's impact on their work. The report provides evidence of AI's integration patterns into knowledge work across different times of day and task types.
